deep.reconstruction:
Context: section I of a manuscript on arrangements of pseudo-lines. Its first item treats arrangements of 3 pseudo-lines, starting from the combinatorial 3-cube and its dual, the octahedron. The goal (completed on the next page) is to obtain the simplest projective arrangement as an antipodal quotient.

Data: a family (Φ_i)_{i∈I} with |I| = 3 and each |Φ_i| = 2. Put Φ = ⊔ Φ_i, so |Φ| = 6, with the projection p: Φ → I. Elements of Φ are the six 2-faces of the cube; elements of I are the three pairs of opposite faces. In coordinates, Φ_i = {+e_i, −e_i}.

Proper faces of the cube correspond to partial sections of p over nonempty subsets of I. Equivalently, they are nonempty A ⊂ Φ with A → I injective. These are the sign vectors in {+,−,0}^3 \ {0}.
- C_2 ≅ Φ: the 6 facets (1-element sets).
- C_1: the 2-element transversals, 3·4 = 12 edges.
- C_0: the 3-element transversals, i.e. full sections, 8 vertices.
Cube incidence is the opposite of inclusion (extension of sections). A vertex lies on a facet iff the facet's singleton is contained in the vertex's 3-set.

The canonical involution a acts as identity on I and as the transposition on each Φ_i. It induces the antipodal map of the cube.

The dual polytope is the octahedron (cross-polytope) with the same index sets, but now incidence is inclusion:
- O_0 = Φ: 6 vertices.
- O_1: 12 edges.
- O_2: 8 triangles.
This is the boundary complex of the cross-polytope: simplices are subsets of Φ containing no antipodal pair.

Next page: quotienting by {1, a} gives the hemi-cube and hemi-octahedron ('projective' or 'grand' cube and octahedron). The hemi-octahedron has 3 vertices, 6 edges and 4 faces. It is identified with the cell decomposition of RP^2 by three lines indexed by I. The line attached to i is the image of the four edges A ↪ I \ {i}, which form two projective edges.

Grothendieck then remarks that the ordinary cube cannot be recovered from the projective figure up to isomorphism. The automorphism groups differ: 48 for the cube versus 24 ≅ S_4 for the hemi-cube, since −1 becomes trivial.

The 3-line case is the base case for describing pseudo-line arrangements as quotients of zonotopal or sign-vector structures.
errors: No mathematical errors. The counts (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices) and the reversal of incidence between cube and octahedron are correct.

Minor point: the empty partial section (the cube itself, sign vector 0) is deliberately excluded, as the inserted 'des parties ≠∅' makes explicit. So the description is of the boundary complex, which is consistent.

ideas.what: Face poset of cube / cross-polytope as partial sections of a 2-to-1 map Φ → I, i.e. transversal subsets of a 'signed' set
ideas.modern_name: Sign vectors / covectors of the coordinate oriented matroid; face lattice of the cube {+,−,0}^n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Coxeter); oriented matroid formalism by Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence (1978)

ideas.what: Antipodal involution acting by transposition in each fibre Φ_i
ideas.modern_name: Antipodal map / central symmetry of centrally symmetric polytopes

ideas.what: Quotient by the antipodal map gives the hemi-cube and hemi-octahedron; the hemi-octahedron equals the arrangement of 3 lines in RP^2 (3 vertices, 6 edges, 4 triangles)
ideas.modern_name: Hemi-octahedron / hemi-cube (abstract regular polytopes {3,4}_3, {4,3}_3); simple arrangement of 3 lines
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coxeter; McMullen–Schulte (abstract regular polytopes); arrangements: Levi 1926, Grünbaum 1972
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses combinatorial regular polyhedra and maps, but not this specific construction as far as I know

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely classical set-up: the cube and octahedron via sign vectors, and their antipodal quotients giving the 3-line arrangement in RP^2. Its only interest is historical. Grothendieck is independently rebuilding oriented-matroid-style combinatorics (partial sections of a double cover Φ → I) around 1981 as groundwork for pseudo-line arrangements.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Ce dernier s'exprime à l'aide d'une famille' rather than 'Le dernier'. The reading is uncertain.
The marginal '(involutif)' seems to be an insertion qualifying the automorphism a ('un automorphisme (involutif) canonique'), not the bijection in the C_0 line.
'transposition (centrale)': the insertion '(centrale)' attaches to the transposition, as transcribed. The phrase is then 'qui induit un automorphisme, encore noté a, du cube (2)'.

Last line: 'mais cette fois-ci la relation d'incidence est celle des prolongements des sections partielles', continuing onto the next page. In context the next page's 'l'involution des parties' should be 'l'inclusion des parties'.
